`reconcileNodePool` exists **twice** on `dshnayder-org/infra` branch `git-access-ab/r10000`, with byte-identical signatures. The vendored copy is the dead one. But **I cannot fully close the build trace**: the branch has no `go.mod`, no `package main`, and no import or call site anywhere, so "which copy the controller binary compiles" cannot be proven end-to-end from this branch.

## The two definitions

Both are free functions (no receiver), identical signature:

`func reconcileNodePool(ctx context.Context, pool *Pool) error`

| Path | Package | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`modules/controller/nodepool.go`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r10000/modules/controller/nodepool.go) `:5` | `controller` | `return reconcile(ctx, pool, "first-party")` |
| [`vendor/upstream-operator/nodepool.go`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r10000/vendor/upstream-operator/nodepool.go) `:5` | `upstream` | `return reconcile(ctx, pool, "vendored")` |

Different packages, so they do not collide. The same duplication exists for `validateQuotaSpec` in `modules/controller/quota.go` and `vendor/upstream-operator/quota.go`.

## Why the vendored copy is dead

Two concrete mechanisms, both from `vendor/upstream-operator/nodepool.go` lines 3–4:

- `// reconcileNodePool is vendored from upstream-operator v0.14.2. Do not edit;`
- `// this copy is not compiled into the controller.`

Plus the path itself: the Go toolchain excludes a top-level `vendor/` tree from package matching (`./...`) unless it is a module's own vendor directory resolving a real import. Nothing on the branch imports `upstream` — a repo-wide search for `import` returns `0` matches. The 400 sibling files `vendor/upstream-operator/gen-000.go` … `gen-399.go` are all `// Code generated by upstream-operator v0.14.2. DO NOT EDIT.`

None of the excluded mechanisms you listed apply: no `//go:build` or `+build` lines (`0` matches repo-wide), no `_test.go` files, no GOOS/GOARCH suffixes.

`modules/controller/` is a **Terraform** module — `part-00.tf` … `part-29.tf`, `resource "meridian_controller"` — with two stray `.go` files in it. There is no `go.mod`, no `func main`, no `import` block, and no definition of `reconcile`, `Pool`, or `context` anywhere on the branch. Neither `.go` file would compile as written. So the verdict "`modules/controller/nodepool.go` is the live copy" rests on the vendoring convention and the file's own comment, **not** on a traced call from a controller main package — that main package does not exist here.
